inspection_summary: V5 has most required components but is not visually converged. The dominant failure is not micro-spacing; it is wrong imagery, missing/incorrect global chrome, underscaled typography/components, and section compositions that differ materially from the approved mockup.

findings.current: Desktop render does not visually reproduce the approved global header and overall premium scale.
findings.reference: Dark Calder header is a strong 45px visual anchor; content below is dense, large and polished.
findings.correction: Reuse the approved homepage header and restore reference-comparable component/type scale.

findings.current: Hero uses black-and-white feet photography; configurator uses bokeh; finish cards use landscapes; recommendations use landscapes/people.
findings.reference: Wheel/product photography dominates hero, configurator, finishes and recommendations; automotive photography dominates Real World; CNC/manufacturing image dominates Engineering.
findings.correction: Stop using fallback/random placeholder media in product contexts. Bind each region to correct asset class.

findings.current: Hero is visually small and sparse with controls compressed into a narrow/lightweight panel.
findings.reference: Hero fills roughly first 515px below breadcrumb; gallery ~57%, info ~43%; large C1 title and substantial configuration panel.
findings.correction: Increase gallery/info scale, typography, control heights and vertical density; use ~57/43 desktop split.

findings.current: Extra functional section is large and visually disconnected from approved mockup.
findings.reference: Approved mockup has no standalone advanced configurator section.
findings.correction: Keep required functionality but compress and style it as an intentional Calder extension; do not let it visually overpower approved PDP sections.

findings.current: Standalone finder is a broad centered band with small controls.
findings.reference: Fitment is primarily a compact pale-green status panel inside hero.
findings.correction: Make hero fitment primary; keep full finder as secondary change/search workflow with reduced visual weight.

findings.current: Top half is a flat blue placeholder labeled Manufacturing Image; bottom is a separate card-like dark block.
findings.reference: Single continuous photographic CNC panel with text overlay and four icon capabilities across bottom.
findings.correction: Use one background image container with gradient overlay; eliminate split placeholder/card composition.

findings.reference: Six large isolated wheel renders on white, labels below, selected wheel outlined gold.
findings.correction: Render finish wheel imagery, not generic images; 6 visible desktop.
Require configured automotive images; hide/flag section in QA if assets absent rather than presenting blank fidelity placeholders.

findings.current: Generic photo cards with Quick Add buttons.
findings.reference: Large wheel renders, model names, construction, price and restrained arrow; no dominant Quick Add.
findings.correction: Use actual shared B1 card and wheel product media.

findings.current: Plain navy block with text concentrated left; little/no image treatment.
findings.reference: Full-width dark image-backed wheel-detail banner, large heading left, gold CTA right, contact methods below.
findings.correction: Use image-backed CTA, two-column desktop layout and approved sizing.

findings.current: Footer content is sparse/small and does not reproduce approved newsletter/social/locale composition.
findings.reference: Substantial dark footer with logo/mission/social, Shop/Explore/Support, Journey newsletter, legal and locale.
findings.correction: Reuse homepage footer component exactly rather than PDP-local approximation.

findings.current: Tablet/mobile inherit underscaled type and generic imagery; mobile sections become long but not visually equivalent.
findings.reference: Responsive version should preserve visual hierarchy and wheel-centric media.
findings.correction: Fix desktop visual system first, then reflow without shrinking typography excessively.
